title: clade-seal promotion gate makes clade-audit output enforceable
problem: After Cycles 13-15 made clade-audit truthful (all hard gates at zero, TODO inventory down to one real finding), the promotion pipeline in clade-promote did not actually run clade-audit or enforce the green state. A truthful self-critic is only valuable if promotion refuses to land when it is not green.
solution: Added a clade-seal binary inside rings/RUST-08/clade-promote that runs clade-audit (JSON), cargo test --workspace, and cargo clippy --workspace; allows a small explicit TODO allow-list by fingerprint; and writes .trinity/state/seal.json. Extended clade-promote to invoke clade-seal as Seal-6 Audit and added --seal-only mode that runs the lightweight seal without requiring a Canary worktree.
result: cargo run --bin clade-seal reports SEAL VALID and writes a passing seal artifact. cargo run --bin clade-promote -- --seal-only --dry-run reports SEAL VALID and skips the swap. A temporary TODO in a test file caused clade-seal to correctly REJECT until removed.
learnings: A truthful self-critic must be wired into promotion to be meaningful. Cycle 16 closed that loop.
Seal artifacts should be machine-readable (JSON) and include git HEAD so the provenance is auditable.
TODO allow-lists should use fingerprints, not line numbers, because line numbers drift.
--seal-only mode is essential for CI/pre-flight because the full Canary build/launch path requires a separate staging worktree.
Argument parsing should explicitly skip flag-style args when selecting positional parameters like clade_id.
mistakes: First implementation of seal.rs contained a TODO comment explaining the allow-list logic; clade-audit correctly flagged it as a disallowed TODO. Auditor source must also be clean.
Initial clade-promote --seal-only path still ran the full Canary build/health/e2e cells and failed because the staging worktree was missing. --seal-only should mean just the lightweight seal cells.
